 Christmas at Cantigny returns for its fourth season Friday, Nov. 20, and runs through Jan. 3 in Wheaton. (Rick West/Daily Herald) 
 Horse-drawn carriage rides return during Long Grove Vintage Holidays, which run Nov. 20 through Dec. 24 in downtown Long Grove. (Brian Hill/Daily Herald) 
 The Aurora Winter Lights Festival will take place Friday, Nov. 20, on Downer Place. (City of Aurora) 
 Rosemont’s Light Up The Park takes place Saturday, Nov. 21, at Parkway Bank Park. The Chicago Wolves Ice Rink at Parkway Bank Park will be open through Jan. 31. (Village of Rosemont) 
 Brookfield Zoo Chicago’s Holiday Magic returns Friday, Nov. 21, through Jan. 3. (Brookfield Zoo Chicago) 
 Palatine’s Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony will take place Saturday, Nov. 21, at Towne Square. (John Starks/Daily Herald) 
 Chazz Palminteri performs “A Bronx Tale” Sunday, Nov. 22, at the Arcada Theatre in St. Charles. (Evan Agostini/Invision/AP) 
 Gary Sinise will take part in a discussion celebrating the release of his new book Monday, Nov. 23, at the McAninch Arts Center in Glen Ellyn. (Mark Humphrey/AP) 
 The Naperville Noon Lions 5K Turkey Trot takes place Thanksgiving morning at Naperville Central High School. (Katlyn Smith/Daily Herald)

Christmas at Cantigny returns for its fourth season Friday, Nov. 20, and runs through Jan. 3 in Wheaton. (Rick West/Daily Herald) 
 Friday, Nov. 20 
 McHenry Festival of Trees: Opening Friday, Nov. 20, and continuing through Dec. 27, at the McHenry Rec Center, 3716 Municipal Drive, McHenry. See holiday trees decorated by local businesses and civic organizations. Vote for your favorite tree with a donation of canned nonperishable food or toiletries for Veteran’s Path to Hope. Open from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. weekdays at the McHenry Rec Center. mchenrychamber.com/festival-of-trees .
 Aurora Christkindlmarket: 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Fridays and Saturdays, 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sundays, and 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Thursdays, from Friday, Nov. 20, through Dec. 24, at RiverEdge Park, 360 N. Broadway, Aurora. Vendors, live entertainment and special events. Free admission. paramountaurora.com .
 Winterland at Gallagher Way: 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Fridays and Saturdays, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Sundays, and 3-9 p.m. Mondays through Thursdays, from Friday, Nov. 20, through Dec. 31, at Gallagher Way, 3635 N. Clark St., Chicago. Holiday hours: 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. Nov. 26. Ice rink, Christkindlmarket, Santa’s Workshop from 4-9 p.m. Fridays and 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturdays and Sundays, Holiday Train, Wreath Workshops and more. Free admission; some activities require a fee. gallagherway.com .
 Millennium Park Holiday Market: Noon to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20-21, and noon to 5 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at Millennium Park, Chase Promenade North, 201 E. Randolph St., Chicago. Shopping, live entertainment and concessions. Free entry. chicago.gov. 
 Barrington Area Artists Association Art Sale: 2-6 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Barrington’s White House, 145 W. Main St., Barrington. Shop for hundreds of fine art pieces from 30 local painters, sculptors and jewelers. Free admission; register at barringtonswhitehouse.com .
 Horse-drawn carriage rides return during Long Grove Vintage Holidays, which run Nov. 20 through Dec. 24 in downtown Long Grove. (Brian Hill/Daily Herald) 
 Long Grove Vintage Holidays: Friday, Nov. 20, through Thursday, Dec. 24, in downtown Long Grove. Horse-drawn carriage rides on weekends, Santa in the village, caroling around town and more. Most events are free; reservations for carriage rides are $15 per seat. longgrove.org/festival/holiday-season. 
 Windy City Invitational Tattoo Convention: 3-10 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20; noon to 10 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21; and noon to 8 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at Palmhouse, 619 Howard St., Evanston. Fourth annual small-scale convention brings together a lineup of American and Japanese traditional tattooers from across the country. Meet the artists, plus vendors, food and drinks. $20 or $30 for a three-day pass. palmhouse619.com/upcoming-events .
 Winter Lights at Central Park: 4-9:30 p.m. daily, from Friday, Nov. 20, through Jan. 3, at Oak Brook Park District Central Park West, 1450 Forest Gate Road, Oak Brook. Thousands of twinkling lights illuminate a half-mile walk through the park. Sensory-friendly from 4-4:30 p.m. when all blinking and moving lights remain static and music is silenced. Do not park on the grass or in nondesignated parking lots. Donations welcome for People’s Resource Center and the Oak Brook Park District Foundation. obparks.org .
 Christmas at Cantigny Light Show: 4:30-9 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Cantigny, 1S151 Winfield Road, Wheaton. And then open from 4:30-9 p.m. Wednesdays through Sundays, from Friday, Nov. 20, to Jan. 3. Closed on Thursday, Nov. 26. New this year is the Sunday night light show, “A Marvelous Christmas,” a light and sound experience inspired by favorite superhero films. Explore the first floor of Col. McCormick’s decorated mansion and see the display of hundreds of poinsettias. Upgrades include the Fireside S’mores for Two ($35) and the Christmas Spirits upgrade ($40), which includes three festive cocktails, each served at exclusive stations along the walk, a special drink in the McCormick House Freedom Hall Bar and a commemorative mug. Advance tickets: $15.99-$25 at cantigny.org .
 McHenry Living Windows and Cocoa Crawl: 4:30-7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, in downtown McHenry. Live mannequins re-create favorite holiday scenes in downtown store windows. It’s paired with a Cocoa Crawl, featuring festive drinks and treats on the trail. Drinks are only for the purchased mugs ($10). Mugs are on sale through Friday, Nov. 20, while supplies last; only 600 mugs available. mchenrychamber.com/living-windows .
 ZooLights: 4:30-9 p.m. select dates Friday, Nov. 20, through Jan. 3, at Lincoln Park Zoo, 2001 N. Clark St., Chicago. More than 3 million lights, including hundreds of luminous LED displays and festive experiences. $7-$20; free on most Mondays. lpzoo.org/event/zoolights. 
 Light Up Long Grove: 5-8 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, in Historic Downtown Long Grove. Vintage Holidays kicks off with tractor-pulled wagon rides, holiday shopping and dining, illuminated photo stations, festive street activities, and the annual Bridge and Tree Lighting Ceremony at 7:30 p.m. with Village President Bill Jacob, followed by a live performance by the Fred Astaire Dancers. Free. longgrove.org/festival/holiday-season. 
 Holiday Lights/Luces Festivas: 5:30-7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Welton Plaza, 4343 Old Grand Ave., Gurnee. A festive holiday light display with horse-drawn trolley rides, a carousel, firepits and s’mores, free pizza, craft stations and more. Special guests include Gurnee Park District Above the Barre Dance Team, Gurnee Mayor Tom Hood and Santa Claus. Free. gurneeparkdistrict.com .
 Holiday Sip & Stroll: 5:30-9 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Brookfield Zoo Chicago, 8400 31st St., Brookfield. Explore the zoo’s holiday lights, plus a DJ dance party, seasonal cocktails and more. For 21 and older. Tickets start at $39.95. brookfieldzoo.org/HolidaySipAndStroll .
 Woman’s Club of Evanston Holiday Bazaar: 5:30-7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20; 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21; and 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at The Woman’s Club, 1702 Chicago Ave., Evanston. Handmade gifts from local artisans. Free entry. wcofe.org. 
 The Aurora Winter Lights Festival will take place Friday, Nov. 20, on Downer Place. (City of Aurora) 
 Aurora Winter Lights Festival: 6-9 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, on Downer Place, from Water Street to River Street, Aurora. At 6:30 p.m., Santa and Mrs. Claus lead the illuminated parade featuring reindeer, elves and special guests. After the parade, Santa and Mrs. Claus, along with the mayor, will light the city’s holiday tree. See a drone light show along the banks of the Fox River. Afterward, on Stolp Avenue, between Downer Place and Galena Boulevard, there will be food vendors, roaming costumed characters and music at Millennium Plaza. This year’s photos with Santa are at a new location: Grand Army of the Republic Military Museum, 23 E. Downer Place. Free. aurora-il.org .
 Carol Stream Holiday Tree Lighting: 6-8 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Ross Ferraro Town Center, 960 N. Gary Ave., Carol Stream. Holiday crafts and activities for kids, performances by the West Chicago High School Choir and local student dance and pom groups, petting zoo, hot cocoa, cookies, seasonal snacks, a visit from Santa Claus and the lighting of the village tree. Free. carolstream.org .
 City of Chicago Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony: 6 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, in Millennium Park, 201 E. Randolph St., Chicago. Chicago’s official Christmas Tree will be lit and remain illuminated through Sunday, Jan. 10. Free. chicago.gov .
 Moonlight Magic: 6-8 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, in downtown Sycamore. Downtown storefronts come alive as local arts, theater and dance groups perform. Shops stay open late for Moonlight Sales & Holiday Magic. facebook.com/SycamoreIllinois .
 Turkey Shoot Free Throw Contest: 6-9 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Techny Prairie Activity Center, 180 Anets Drive, Northbrook. Shoot free throws and win a turkey for first place in each age division. Second place receives a pie. $9 for Northbrook residents, $14 for nonresidents. nbparks.org .
 “Shrek the Musical Jr.”: 6:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, and 2 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, Nov. 21-22, at Ray Morrill Community Center, Memorial Room, 1777 S. Blanchard Road, Wheaton. Children’s Playhouse production. Tickets are $10 at wheatonparkdistrict.com .
 Charles Dickens’ “A Christmas Carol”: 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, and 2 and 5 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, Nov. 21-29, at Belushi Performance Hall, 425 Fawell Blvd., Glen Ellyn. College of DuPage Theater’s family-friendly 70-minute show featuring a cast of 50 local actors and children. $18-$20. a tthemac.org/events/a-christmas-carol. 
 “Explore the Sound”: 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Wentz Concert Hall, 171 College Ave., Naperville. Annual choral event features Chamber Singers, Chorale and Concert Choir, with collaborative pianist and guest instrumental artists in a staged and theatrically lit concert. $7. northcentralcollege.edu/show/calendar .
 Marc Maron: 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at The Vic Theatre, 3145 N. Sheffield Ave., Chicago. “Yammering Into the Void Tour.” Tickets start at $111. jamusa.com. 
 Nurse John: 7 and 10 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at the Chicago Theatre, 175 N. State St., Chicago. “Against Medical Advice.” Tickets start at $46.90. msg.com. 
 “Santa Switch”: 7 p.m. Fridays, Nov. 20 through Dec. 4; 1 and 7 p.m. Saturdays, Nov. 21 and Dec. 5; 1 and 4 p.m. Sundays, Nov. 22 and Dec. 6; and 7 p.m. Thursday, Dec. 3, at the Raue Center for the Arts, 26 N. Williams St., Crystal Lake. A holiday jukebox musical by Raue Center School for the Arts students and adults. $10.50-$40. rauecenter.org .
 “Cabaret”: 7:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20-21, and 2 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at The Lodge Performing Arts Center, 18 Villa Court, Elgin. Up and Coming Theatre’s fall production of Kander & Ebb’s classic musical. $30.15 for onstage table seating or $27 for main seating. uactheatre.org. 
 Camerata Chicago “Messiah”: 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Nineteenth Century Club, 178 Forest Ave., Oak Park; 3 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Gary United Methodist Church, 224 N. Main St., Wheaton; and 3 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at Union Church of Hinsdale, 137 S. Garfield St., Hinsdale. Handel’s “Messiah” Part 1, with sing-along “Hallelujah” chorus and “Zadok the Priest.” The Camerata Chicago Orchestra and Chorus will perform the “Hallelujah Chorus.” It will be performed twice, with the audience joining in the second time. $50, $40 for 65 and older, $10 for students, and $2 for 14 and younger. VIP tickets: $75. CamerataChicago.org .
 Children’s Theatre of Elgin “The Little Mermaid Jr.”: 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20; 11 a.m. and 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21; and 2 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at the Hemmens, 45 Symphony Way, Elgin. $14-$16. cteelgin.com/shows .
 CLC Winter Dance Concert: 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, and 2 and 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, in the Mainstage Theatre at the College of Lake County, 19351 W. Washington St., Grayslake. $11-$13. jlcenter.clcillinois.edu .
 ECC Theatre’s “The Man Who Came to Dinner”: 7:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20-21, and 3 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at Elgin Community College’s SecondSpace, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin. When an egotistical, urbane critic gets stranded in a Midwestern town, it sets off a three-ring circus of farcical machinations and celebrity satire. $14-$16; free for ECC students with ID. eccartscenter.org .
 ESO Presents String Trio: 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Journey of Hope United Methodist Church, 37W040 Highland Ave., Elgin. $15-$25. elginsymphony.org .
 The Fabulous Equinox Orchestra: 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Elgin Community College Blizzard Theater, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin. “Broadway to Bourbon Street” fuses Broadway hits with the soulful energy of New Orleans, including favorites from “Guys and Dolls,” “West Side Story,” “Hairspray” and more. Pre-show dinner, prepared by ECC culinary students, at 5 p.m. at Spartan Terrace Restaurant for $35; wine and beer for purchase. Show tickets: $45. tickets.eccartscenter.org .
 “Hedda Gabler”: 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, and 2 and 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Elmhurst University’s Mill Theatre, 253 Walter St., Elmhurst. $5-$15. elmhurst.edu .
 “It’s A Wonderful Life — A Live Radio Play”: Previews at 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, and 3 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21; regular run opens at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, and runs various times Fridays through Sundays, and select Wednesdays and Thursdays, through Dec. 27, at Oil Lamp Theater, 1723 Glenview Road, Glenview. Return to WBFR Studios to journey to Bedford Falls, where George Bailey’s troubles lead him to wish he was never born, complete with live sound effects, radio jingles and more. $55. oillamptheater.org .
 “She Loves Me”: 7:30 p.m. Fridays, Saturdays and Thursdays and 2 p.m. Sundays, Nov. 20 through Dec. 13, except Thursday, Nov. 26, at Playhouse 111, 111 N. Hale St., Wheaton. Wheaton Drama’s production of the romantic musical comedy. $25. wheatondrama.org .
 Wheaton College Jazz Ensemble and Combos Fall Concert: 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at the Armerding Center for Music and the Arts Concert Hall, 520 E. Kenilworth Ave., Wheaton. A large Jazz Ensemble and smaller Showcase Combos perform a range of music. $5.90-$11.80. tickets.wheaton.edu .
 Friday Night Concert Series: 8 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, at Two Way Street Coffee House, 1047 Curtiss St., Downers Grove. Aaron LaCombe will perform. Doors open at 7:30 p.m., or tune in virtually. Suggested donation $10 (cash or PayPal). twowaystreet.org. 
 “Second City Nut-Cracking Holiday Revue”: 8 p.m. Fridays, 3 and 8 p.m. Saturdays, and 3 p.m. Sundays, Nov. 20 through Dec. 23, at the Copley Theatre, 8 E. Galena Blvd., Aurora. A fast-paced, interactive comedy revue stuffed with seasonal songs, sketches and improv comedy. $52.38. paramountaurora.com .
 “ Cleopatra, The Immersive Exhibition”: Various times and days Friday, Nov. 20, through Monday, Jan. 4, at EXP Rosemont, 9900 Berwyn Ave., Rosemont. Discover the life, legacy and mythology of Cleopatra VII through a multisensory journey into ancient Egypt and Rome. Tickets start at $36. exprosemont.com .
 Saturday, Nov. 21 
 Tom-A-Hawk Turkey Trot 5K: 8 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, in front of Jake’s Bagels, 220 N. Broadway, Aurora, and crossing the Fox River from west to east over the pedestrian bridge. Sixth annual run to benefit A+ Foundation for West Aurora Schools and the Aurora East Educational Foundation. $40; $25 for 18 and younger. runsignup.com/Race/IL/Aurora/TomAHawk5k .
 Island Lake Holiday Craft Fair: 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, Nov. 21-22, at the village hall, 3720 Greenleaf Ave., Island Lake. Gifts, holiday decor, jewelry, crafts and more. Free admission. villageofislandlake.com .
 Photos with Santa: 9:15 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at the Lake Ellyn Boathouse in Glen Ellyn. Spend time with Santa and the Elves, plus there will be treats, hot cocoa and crafts while a photographer captures the moments. Families can register for one 10-minute time slot. Glen Ellyn Parks Foundation fundraiser. Register: geparksfoundation.org/events .
 International Holiday Market: 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Estonian House of Chicago, 14700 Estonian Lane, Riverwoods. Crafts, food and gifts from around the world, jewelry, handmade items, soaps, ornaments, bonfire, Glogg and more. $5, free for kids younger than 16. facebook.com/chicagoeestimaja .
 Photos With Santa: 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, and 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at the historic Nancy Kimball Cobblestone House, 302 W. Chicago St., Elgin. Book a 15-minute time block to take photos with Santa. Pets and props are welcome. Craft activity and snacks available in the basement. $30. Register: elginhistory.org .
 Rudolph Run/Walk: 10 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Mooseheart Field House, 155 S. International Drive, Batavia. Fifth annual run, walk or stroll to benefit Mooseheart Child City & School and Moosehaven Senior Living Community. Virtual option available. $40, $20 for 12 and younger. Register: mooseintl.org/rudolph-run-5k-walk .
 Family Holiday Movies: 10:30 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Glen Art Theatre, 540 Crescent Blvd., Glen Ellyn. See “The Lego Movie.” Doors open at 10 a.m. Free. glenellynchamber.com/free-family-movies .
 Campton Township’s Christmas at Corron Farm: 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Corron Farm, 7N761 Corron Road, St. Charles. Family-friendly event featuring photos with Santa, an indoor holiday market, crafts at the children’s table, s’mores over a fire pit, hot cocoa, cider doughnuts and live caroling. Free. camptontownship.com. 
 Rosemont’s Light Up The Park takes place Saturday, Nov. 21, at Parkway Bank Park. The Chicago Wolves Ice Rink at Parkway Bank Park will be open through Jan. 31. (Village of Rosemont) 
 Chicago Wolves Ice Rink at Parkway Bank Park: 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, in the Parkway Bank Park Entertainment District, 5501 Park Place, Rosemont. The rink will open for ice skating leading up to the park’s “Light Up The Park” tree-lighting celebration from 2-6 p.m., which includes meet-and-greets with Santa and Mrs. Claus, horse-drawn sleigh rides, carolers and ice-sculpting demonstrations. The rink will remain open through Jan. 31. Free; skate rental is $8. rosemont.com/thepark. 
 The Wintrust Magnificent Mile Lights Festival: 11 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Pioneer Court, 401 N. Michigan Ave., Chicago. Lights Festival Lane offers a festive outdoor celebration with live entertainment, music and family-friendly activities from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. The parade on North Michigan Avenue will feature Grand Marshals Mickey Mouse and Minnie Mouse, with floats, marching bands, giant helium balloons, Santa Claus and more. The Wintrust Fireworks Spectacular takes place at 7:30 p.m. Free. themagnificentmile.com/lights-festival .
 Downtown McHenry Holiday Walk: Noon to 5 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Veteran’s Memorial Park, 3400 Pearl St., McHenry. From noon to 4 p.m., visit Santa in the gazebo and take a horse-drawn sleigh ride around the park. There will be Kids Build-It kits, games and crafts. At 4:30 p.m., McHenry High School Vocal Warriors will lead caroling, with the ceremony at 5 p.m. lighting up thousands of twinkling lights in the park and around the downtown streets. Free. m chenrychamber.com/downtown-holiday-walk. 
 Barrington Dance Ensemble Presents Clara’s Nutcracker Tea: 1 and 3 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Barrington’s White House, 145 W. Main St., Barrington. Character performances, interactive dancing, photo opportunities and vintage holiday treats donated by Ambrosia Euro-American Pâtisserie. Attendees will receive complimentary raffle tickets for a chance to win four tickets to BDE’s performance of “The Nutcracker.” $55.20. barringtonswhitehouse.com .
 Train Saturdays: 1:30-3:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at the DuPage County Historical Museum auditorium, 102 E. Wesley St., Wheaton. See an HO-scale model train operated by the DuPage Society of Model Engineers. Detailed layout covers more than 2,000 feet of track and highlights some of DuPage County’s railroads and landmarks. Suggested donation: $5, $2 for kids and seniors. dupagemuseum.org .
 An Almost Winter Day: 2-5 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at SEBA Park, 151 S. Water St., South Elgin. Activities include a s’more station, cookie decorating, balloon animals, craft station, snowball slingshot, letters to Santa, tree-decorating contest, ice sculptor and concessions. Pictures with Santa from 2-4:45 p.m.; bring a camera. Village tree lighting at 5 p.m. at Panton Mill Park. southelgin.com .
 Light Up The Park: 2-6 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Parkway Bank Park, 5501 Park Place, Rosemont. Visits with Santa and Mrs. Claus, free horse-drawn sleigh rides, carolers, skating and ice-sculpting. Rosemont Mayor Brad Stephens will arrive at 5:30 p.m. to illuminate the park with more than 80,000 holiday lights. Free. rosemont.com/thepark .
 Brookfield Zoo Chicago’s Holiday Magic returns Friday, Nov. 21, through Jan. 3. (Brookfield Zoo Chicago) 
 Brookfield Zoo Chicago’s Holiday Magic: 3-9 p.m. Nov. 21-25 and 27-29, Dec. 3-6, 10-13, 17-23 and 26-31, and Jan. 1-3, at Brookfield Zoo Chicago, 8400 31st St., Brookfield. Explore themed areas filled with larger-than-life holiday displays, interactive experiences, glowing tunnels, a maze and animal-themed light displays. Dance at the Retro Christmas dance area and shop the Holiday Market. Santa visits on select nights. Sensory-friendly Holiday Magic on Dec. 3. $20.95-$29.95. brookfieldzoo.org/HolidayMagic .
 Wood Dale Tree Lighting : 3-5 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at city hall, 404 N. Wood Dale Road, Wood Dale. Santa visits, face painting and crafts before the annual tree lighting ceremony. Collection site for Toys for Tots. Free. wooddale.com .
 Woodridge Winterfest: 3-6 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Kagann Plaza at the village hall, 5 Plaza Drive, Woodridge. Features the 20-foot Christmas tree-lighting ceremony at 5 p.m., festive photos with Santa, a maker’s market, holiday trolley rides, food trucks and vendors, festive holiday music with Celebration Brass, a kids’ craft area, and character meet-and-greets. For parking, see woodridgeil.gov. 
 Highland Park Holiday Lighting: 4-6 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Port Clinton Square, 600-601 Central Ave., Highland Park. Santa and Hanukkah Harry, live music from DJ Julian, Frozen Robins Carolers, dance performances, free popcorn and hot cocoa, and festive photo opportunities, including a new America250 Tree, giant sleigh and inflatable snow globe. Write letters to Santa and enjoy candy canes from Santa and chocolate gelt from Hanukkah Harry. Dancers from North Shore School of Dance and A Time to Dance will perform. Free. cityhpil.com .
 Noël Lounge at the McCormick House: 4-10 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, and Wednesdays through Sundays, Nov. 22 through Jan. 4, in Noël Lounge at the McCormick House at Cantigny, 1S151 Winfield Road, Wheaton. Also open 4-10 p.m. Mondays and Tuesdays, Dec. 22-30. Closed on Nov. 27, Dec. 23-24 and Dec. 31-Jan. 1. Experience the pop-up lounge in the elegant second-floor rooms with artisanal shareable small plates from the chef’s menu alongside the curated wine list and signature craft cocktails. $20 booking deposit per person. Christmas at Cantigny Light Show purchase required. Tickets: cantigny.org .
 Palatine’s Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony will take place Saturday, Nov. 21, at Towne Square. (John Starks/Daily Herald) 
 Palatine Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony: 4:45-7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at Towne Square, Slade and Greeley streets, Palatine. Santa visits and pictures in the Towne Square gazebo, holiday music and more. Free. palatine.il.us. 
 ArtWauk: 5-9 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, in the Arts & Entertainment District, 2001 Belvedere Road, Waukegan. The monthly celebration of arts in downtown Waukegan and the Belvidere Mall includes art exhibits, musicians and performances. Free. artwauk.com .
 Hoffman Estates Friendship Tree Lighting: 5-8 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at the village hall, 1900 Hassell Road, Hoffman Estates. Free. hoffmanestates.org .
 Holiday Murder Mystery Dinner: 6-9 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at the ARC Center, 201 W. National St., West Chicago. “The Most Wonderful Crime of the Year” is a murder-mystery dinner event with a buffet dinner and cash bar. For 21 and older. Free childcare for kids 3-13 available with pre-registration, including pizza and activities. $50-$60. Register: we-goparks.org/special-events .
 Polar Express Pub Crawl: 6-10:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, in downtown McHenry. From 6-7 p.m., 21 and older can get a “train ticket” for $20 from the McHenry Area Chamber office, 1307 N.
